title: How to build an AI model to recognize objects
reading: The slide frames object recognition as a classifier: a robot 'sees a picture' and 'tells the object class', formalized as an image-in / label-out block diagram, with the classifier internals shown as a neural network. The caption describes the model as a sequence of "learnable" computation.

visuals.description: Robot icon with yellow arrows labelled 'See a picture' (in) and 'Tell the object class' (out); below, a pipeline: Image → black box labelled 'Classifier' → Label (e.g., dog or cat).
visuals.assertion: Object recognition is a function mapping an input image to a class label, performed by a classifier.

visuals.description: Sketch of a fully connected feedforward neural network with red input nodes, four columns of blue hidden nodes, and two green output nodes, with a legend Input/Hidden/Output.
visuals.assertion: The classifier is implemented as a multi-layer neural network, i.e. a sequence of learnable computations.

concepts.why_it_matters: Core abstraction mapping images to labels.

concepts.why_it_matters: Emphasizes parameters fitted from data rather than hand-coded rules.
